module purpose: neorv32_spi is an SPI controller accessible over a bus: it accepts bus writes to configure control registers and enqueue TX data into a TX FIFO, drives SPI signals (spi_clk_o, spi_dat_o, spi_csn_o) to perform transfers, captures incoming SPI bits into an RX FIFO, and produces bus responses and an interrupt output (irq_o).

use-case flows.value: write control registers (enable, cpha, cpol, prsc, cdiv, highspeed, irq enables) from bus_req_i.data
enqueue a TX FIFO entry from a bus write which the transceiver consumes to begin or continue an SPI transfer
SPI byte transfer: clock generation, chip-select control, bit shifts out (spi_dat_o) and sampling in (spi_dat_i) driven by the transceiver FSM
generate an interrupt (irq_o) when enabled conditions (RX available, TX empty/half, idle) occur
return control/status fields and RX FIFO data on bus reads via bus_rsp_o.data
hardware reset clears control registers, transceiver state and counters, resets SPI outputs and FIFOs when rstn_i = '0'

conceptual assets.concept: Control register settings (enable, cpha, cpol, prsc, cdiv, highspeed, IRQ enables) that determine SPI timing, phase/polarity, enabling and IRQ masks
conceptual assets.reasoning: The bus_access process writes these fields from bus_req_i.data when a bus write to the control register space occurs (assignments at lines 140-149). The map shows bus_req_i.data has SOURCES records at those assignment occurrences (for example bus_req_i.data occurrence 2 line 140 SOURCES -> ctrl.enable) and the ctrl fields are stored as registers (CLOCKED_BY on their assignment occurrences, e.g. ctrl.enable occurrence 3 line 140 CLOCKED_BY -> clk_i). The same ctrl fields are consumed by clock_generator (ctrl.prsc/ctrl.cdiv/ctrl.highspeed select and constrain cdiv_cnt/spi_clk_en at lines 371-376) and by the transceiver (ctrl.enable sets rtx_engine.state(2) at line 281; ctrl.cpha/cpol affect rtx_engine.sck at lines 299-324). Because these stored values directly control transfer timing, enabling and IRQ masking, the RTL establishes an integrity property for the control settings.

conceptual assets.concept: TX FIFO contents (bus-written transmit bytes and CS-control words) that determine what the transceiver sends
conceptual assets.reasoning: Bus writes push TX entries (tx_fifo.we is asserted by the bus write condition at line 212; tx_fifo.wdata is driven from bus_req_i.data at line 213). The FIFO instance presents data back to this module (tx_fifo.rdata connected from the sub-unit at line 207) and the transceiver reads tx_fifo.rdata in state "100" to load cs_ctrl or sreg and continue transfers (lines 288-294). Map records show tx_fifo.we is GATED_BY at tx_fifo.we occurrence 3 line 212 (guarded by bus_req_i.stb/rw/addr), tx_fifo.wdata DERIVES_FROM at tx_fifo.wdata occurrence 3 line 213 -> bus_req_i.data, and tx_fifo.rdata is delivered by the sub-unit connection tx_fifo_inst.rdata_o (connection at tx_fifo.rdata occurrence 2 line 207). Because the transceiver's loaded value comes from the FIFO, the integrity and availability of TX FIFO contents are established by these RTL statements.

conceptual assets.concept: RX FIFO contents (received bytes stored for bus readback)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The transceiver writes completed received bytes into the RX FIFO (rx_fifo.wdata <= '0' & rtx_engine.sreg at line 244; rx_fifo.we <= rtx_engine.done at line 245), and those words are returned to the bus on reads (bus_rsp_o.data <- rx_fifo.rdata at line 174). The map shows rx_fifo.wdata DERIVES_FROM rtx_engine.sreg at rx_fifo.wdata occurrence 3 line 244, rx_fifo.we COPIES rtx_engine.done at rx_fifo.we occurrence 3 line 245, and rx_fifo.rdata is connected from the fifo instance (rx_fifo_inst.rdata_o at rx_fifo.rdata occurrence 3 line 239). Therefore received data stored in RX FIFO is a stored asset whose integrity matters for correct readout and whose availability matters for delivering received bytes.

conceptual assets.concept: Transceiver FSM and shift-register state (rtx_engine.state, rtx_engine.sreg, bit counter, sampled bit) that implement an ongoing SPI transfer
conceptual assets.reasoning: The transceiver process implements the transfer state machine and updates the shift register and bit counter on clock edges (rtx_engine.state assignments and shift operations are in the transceiver process, lines 266-336; e.g. rtx_engine.state(2) <= ctrl.enable at line 281; sampling and shifting at lines 308-326). The sampled input spi_dat_i is captured into rtx_engine.sdi_sync (line 310) and rtx_engine.sreg drives spi_dat_o and is used to produce rx_fifo.wdata (lines 318-244, 343). Map records show spi_dat_i CARRIES to rtx_engine.sdi_sync at spi_dat_i occurrence 2 line 310, rtx_engine.sreg has CLOCKED_BY at occurrence 4 line 292, rtx_engine.state has CLOCKED_BY at occurrence 4 line 281, and spi_dat_o and spi_clk_o are driven from rtx_engine.sreg and rtx_engine.sck (spi_dat_o DERIVES_FROM occurrence 2 line 343 target rtx_engine.sreg; spi_clk_o COPIES occurrence 2 line 344 target rtx_engine.sck). The FSM state and shift register are therefore primary assets whose integrity determines transmitted/received bits and control of the SPI signals.

conceptual assets.concept: Chip-select outputs (spi_csn_o) driven by rtx_engine.cs_ctrl selecting which slave is activated
conceptual assets.reasoning: The chip_select process writes spi_csn_o each clock and drives one bit low when rtx_engine.cs_ctrl(3) = '1' using the index rtx_engine.cs_ctrl(2 downto 0) (lines 347-355; selected assignment at line 354). The map records spi_csn_o SELECTED_BY at occurrence 4 line 354 targeting rtx_engine.cs_ctrl and shows rtx_engine.cs_ctrl is driven from tx_fifo.rdata (rtx_engine.cs_ctrl derives from tx_fifo.rdata at occurrence 4 line 290 and is clocked at line 290). Therefore the mapping from FIFO-coded CS-control words into spi_csn_o is an established integrity asset: corrupt cs_ctrl or FIFO rdata yields a wrong CS.

conceptual assets.concept: Interrupt output decision (irq_o) computed from control IRQ enables and FIFO/transceiver status
conceptual assets.reasoning: The irq_generator computes irq_o as ctrl.enable AND an OR of enabled event flags (assignment at line 255; uses ctrl.irq_rx_avail, ctrl.irq_tx_empty, ctrl.irq_tx_nhalf, ctrl.irq_idle and fifo/engine status at lines 255-259). Map shows irq_o DERIVES_FROM at occurrence 3 line 255 with targets including ctrl.irq_idle and ctrl.irq_rx_avail; ctrl.irq_rx_avail is a stored register (CLOCKED_BY at ctrl.irq_rx_avail occurrence 3 line 146 -> clk_i), and rx_fifo.avail and tx_fifo.avail appear as SOURCES to irq_o (rx_fifo.avail occurrence 4 line 256 SOURCES -> irq_o; tx_fifo.avail occurrence 5 line 257 SOURCES -> irq_o). Because irq_o is an output that the RTL computes from these stored settings and statuses, its correctness (integrity) and its availability when conditions occur are established by the RTL.

conceptual assets.concept: SPI clock-enable (spi_clk_en) that gates transceiver bit shifts and timing
conceptual assets.reasoning: The clock_generator produces spi_clk_en and cdiv_cnt under ctrl.enable and either clkgen_i(indexed by ctrl.prsc) or ctrl.highspeed; when cdiv_cnt equals ctrl.cdiv the generator asserts spi_clk_en for one cycle (lines 362-377). The map records show spi_clk_en stored by clock (CLOCKED_BY at spi_clk_en occurrence 6 line 368 -> clk_i), ctrl.prsc SELECTS and clkgen_i GATES the generation condition (ctrl.prsc SELECTS at occurrence 5 line 371 targets spi_clk_en; clkgen_i GATES at occurrence 2 line 371 targets spi_clk_en). Transceiver state transitions and bitcount increments are gated by spi_clk_en (map shows spi_clk_en GATES rtx_engine.bitcnt and other rtx_engine fields), so spi_clk_en's integrity is established by the RTL as it determines when bits are shifted and sampled.
